West Virginia

3 directory entries · Research in progress

  • Mingo↗Historical conflict / regional connection
    Connection & source
    Historical conflict / regional connection

    The article directly connects people described historically as Mingo with conflicts involving West Virginia settlements. It locates many participants' home villages in Pennsylvania or Ohio and explains the label's mixed, changing use. The link therefore records historical activity involving this region, not a resident Mingo state-wide homeland or a present single government. Inspection: Full short article, especially the paragraph on West Virginia settlements and discussion of the historical name.

    Eighteenth-century Ohio Valley; explicitly documented connection to West Virginia settlements in the 1770s. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Shawnee↗Historical regional connection
    Connection & source
    Historical regional connection

    The specialist overview explicitly identifies Shawnee among peoples historically associated with Western Virginia and discusses hunting, travel and regional influence. The separate Chief Logan article locates Shawnee participation at Point Pleasant in 1774. This is a historical connection, not a claim of exclusive state-wide occupation or present government location. Inspection: Actual historical-regional paragraphs; Chief Logan article's 1774 Point Pleasant paragraph as corroboration.

    Early historic/colonial Ohio Valley and Western Virginia connections; 1774 event provides a specific example. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗ · Supporting source 1 ↗
  • Susquehannock↗Reported historical displacement connection
    Connection & source
    Reported historical displacement connection

    The community account cautiously reports evidence suggesting displaced Susquehannock people inhabited West Virginia. Maslowski's specialist overview also names Susquehannock among historically associated groups. Retain the source's uncertainty: this is a reported displacement connection, not a verified continuous settlement, exclusive homeland boundary or present legal title. Inspection: Actual three-paragraph historical-territory account; e-WV's named historical-group paragraph as supporting context.

    Displacement after Conestoga Town's destruction; community page supplies no precise settlement dates. Reviewed 2026-10-21.
